_why: Rules 7 and 8 (#25) are prose that GATES, so the gate has to be shown to bite. Every mutation carries its own `test` key: a battery scored on the whole file cannot tell a kill from a wrong-catcher, and two of these were caught by the wrong assertion on the first pass -- see the-prescription-verb-goes-soft.

mutations.name: rule-7-gate-loses-its-exit
mutations._mechanism: `set -e` is inert in the Bash tool's top-level shell, so a bare call that exits 1 falls through and commits the artifact the gate just refused.

mutations.name: rule-7-gates-after-the-commit
mutations._mechanism: A second gate run proves the freeze only if the commit sits BETWEEN the two runs. Moved after, it certifies content already committed.

mutations.name: rule-7-command-uses-an-unbound-var
mutations._mechanism: Rule 6's first draft prescribed `--message-file "$MSG"` with $MSG bound nowhere: a command that reads correctly and cannot be run. The same trap one rule later.

mutations.name: rule-8-stops-naming-rule-5
mutations._mechanism: Rule 5's failure is a report never read; rule 8's is a report read and TRUSTED. Without the explicit contrast a reader folds the two and thinks rule 5 already covers it.
mutations.find: This is the exact inverse of rule 5's failure
mutations.replace: This is the exact inverse of the earlier failure

mutations.name: the-prescription-verb-goes-soft
mutations._mechanism: SURVIVED TWICE before the guard was fixed. `"re-read" in section.lower()` matched the cited evidence -- the wsg orchestrator saying it 'never re-read the FR' -- so the string was present whatever the prescription said. Scoping to bold spans was still not enough while the section anchor was a PREFIX of the bold heading: the dangling `**` pairs with the next one and shifts every span by one, swallowing the italic quote into span 1. Fixed by anchoring on the complete heading.
mutations.find:
re-read the section that carried it in the
   revised document
mutations.replace:
consult the section that carried it in the
   revised document

mutations.name: two-spelled-counts-in-one-intro
mutations._mechanism: The count test derives the expected number from the spelled word. Two spelled counts must be AMBIGUOUS rather than silently first-wins, or the derivation reintroduces the staleness it replaced.
